“But the reception here is bad, so I can't really make calls.”
“I just feel like you're a bit down.”
Even though she says that, I can't help but feel that Kasumi is a bit out of spirits.
And it seems like she's been like this a few days a week.
“Can I ask you something, from a boy's perspective?”
“Sure, but saying 'boy' might be a bit...”
“If you broke up with your girlfriend, would you still want to keep in touch with her?”
“No, no, no, no, it's not me—it's a... yeah, a friend!”
“Yes, yes, she came to me for advice and wanted to know what you think.”
“There are pleasant and unpleasant breakups, and even more complicated scenarios.”
“So what was the situation with your... friend?”
“It was... she who initiated the breakup... my friend said that.”
“From what I've observed, if it's an amicable breakup, people usually keep in touch.”
“Yeah... I used to assist a counseling psychologist, who dealt with a lot of relationship issues.”
“Oh... you really are an experienced man!”
“Uh... Y-Yeah! Haha... You can count on me for anything!”
“Hehe, then I'll be relying on you a lot, {Me}!”
“If the breakup was due to some conflict, then the chances of staying in touch are pretty low.”
But it's not really my place to interfere...
Still, I hate to see Kasumi look so sad.
“This is the perfect time for meat!”
“I was planning to use it for dinner, but I think it's better to use it now.”
“Let's get started before the grill gets too hot, Kasumi.”
“I saw some in the fridge earlier, so I got some for you.”
“Ayano and Shizuku don't seem like drinkers.”
“Kasumi, you're the kind who drinks alone, I can tell!”
“The grill's hot... Now let's start grilling!”
The sizzling sound of the meat on the grill makes our mouths water.
And boy does that smell good!
“When you're feeling down, a BBQ is guaranteed to cheer you up!”
“And with a cool beer, isn't it just perfect?!”
“Whatever~ We can do this every once in a while!”
Kasumi watches the meat on the grill intently, sipping beer.
Though subtle, I see her swallowing in anticipation.
I put the finished ribs on a plate, cut them into pieces, and hand them to Kasumi.
“Of course, no wonder it smells so good!”
“There's another piece ready here, I'll cut it up, and let's invite Shizuku too.”
“Chocolate with this? That would be such a waste!”
“If Shizuku won't eat it, I will!”
And just like that, the afternoon turned into an impromptu barbecue party.
Seeing everyone so happy made me feel good too. It was nice to lift everyone's spirits, including my own.
Kasumi quietly approaches me and softly calls my name.
Suddenly, a piece of perfectly cut rib finds its way into my mouth.
“Thank you. I feel a lot better now.”
Kasumi opens a can of beer and hands it to me.
“Can't have a barbecue without beer, right?”
